tasks.task: Build an asset and vehicle register

items.when: When the client has a rough list of kit and vehicles and needs one register with IDs, intervals and owners
When an old asset list is handed over, to find gaps, duplicates and odd values before you build on it
When the fields are agreed and you need a clean, formatted workbook with no made-up rows
When staff will add assets themselves and need dropdowns and entry checks to keep the list clean
When the register lives in Excel and the client wants to query and update it in the sheet

tasks.task: Build a preventive maintenance calendar

items.when: When the register is in place and each service needs a date, an owner and the source of its interval
When you have repair history, to draw service intervals and a spares list from what really fails
When money or hours cannot cover every service, to compare two plans with costs and dates
When deciding what to service often and what to leave: parts that wear fast against things that last

tasks.task: Set up planned maintenance where there is no system

items.when: When there is no system, a tool was bought and never filled, or a new site or fleet is taken on
When the client is choosing a maintenance or fleet tool, to score the options against their needs
When moving from a spreadsheet or an old tool, to switch in stages without losing open jobs

tasks.task: Write daily check sheets for equipment

items.when: When each equipment type needs a one-page check with tick boxes and what a fail looks like
When checks should be done on a phone, with each fail emailed to the right person and logged
When a sheet uses office words, to rewrite it in the words the crew say and test it read aloud
When sheets come back ticked but faults are missed, to find what makes the check hard to do right

tasks.task: Write a vehicle walkaround check and defect route

items.when: When drivers need a one-page daily check and defects must reach the person who can act
When a reported defect must become a work order with a priority and a close-out
When drivers will report on a phone and a defect must send an alert the same minute

tasks.task: Turn fault reports into work orders and keep the log

items.when: When a fault arrives as a text, email or shout and needs a clear work order with a priority
When there is no work order form or log that tracks each fault from report to close
When reports arrive in many forms with fields missing, to set one intake procedure and checks
When the log has dates and you need monthly counts, totals and rates you can trace to rows

tasks.task: Review an overdue maintenance backlog

items.when: When a pile of overdue services needs sorting into do first, reschedule and drop
When open repair tickets pile up, to list overdue decisions and what each needs to close
When the backlog keeps growing, to go and watch the work and find where jobs wait

tasks.task: Run the weekly maintenance review

items.when: At the start of each week, to review open work orders, checks done and services due
When the owner wants one page each week with status, risks and the decisions needed
Before the weekly figures go out, to catch broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Build the statutory checks calendar for a site

items.when: When fire, water, lifting, gas and electrical check dates sit in different heads and files
Before sharing, to make sure every date and interval has a dated source or is cut
Each month, to catch service contracts and notice dates due before a statutory visit lapses

tasks.task: Set up water temperature and flushing logs

items.when: When the written scheme lists routine checks and you need a log sheet and a monthly summary
When the water checks must sit on the same calendar as the site's other statutory dates
When readings are typed into Excel and out-of-range entries should be flagged as they are made
When a month of readings needs a summary with counts of misses and out-of-range results

tasks.task: Brief a contractor and manage the job to sign-off

items.when: When a work order needs an outside contractor, from request through quote to sign-off
Before a contractor comes on site, to set out the job, site risks, permits and access
When building work ends, to turn inspection notes into a defects list with owners and proof
When a contractor job closes, to keep proof of what was delivered and what is still open

tasks.task: Compare contractor quotes and service contracts

items.when: When two or more contractor proposals need one cost and risk table in plain words
When price is not the only test, to weight response time, cover and skills and get one pick
When a service contract is up for renewal, to plan notice dates and keep, renegotiate or replace
When the owner must choose, to give one memo with the options, risks and missing facts

tasks.task: Track contractor performance and renewals

items.when: When a contractor misses response times, to score them and get a keep, review or replace call
Each month, to see which contractors to keep, whose terms to fix and which agreements to redo
Each month, to list renewals and notice dates due and the traps in each

tasks.task: Decide whether to repair or replace an asset

items.when: When an asset keeps failing and you have its repair history, running costs and a quote
When a replacement is a big purchase, to work out payback, return and risk
Before the figures go to the owner, to catch formula errors and broken links in the workbook
When the owner signs off the spend, to put the choice, risks and missing facts on one memo

tasks.task: Plan fleet size and vehicle replacement

items.when: When the client asks how many vehicles they need and when each should be replaced
When there is a replacement quote and a sale value, to compare keeping and replacing in cash
When the vehicle is a truck that earns per trip, to set trip earnings beside replacement
When one vehicle's repair bills are the trigger, to test the case on its own history
When the fleet can be renewed all at once or in steps, to compare two plans with money and dates

tasks.task: Find why a breakdown keeps coming back

items.when: When the same fault returns, to build a chain of whys checked against facts, with a fix
When the team must review a failure together, to set who attends and a no-blame agenda
When the causes are known, to size a fix at each level with an owner, date and check
When the cause is argued from the office, to go to the machine and look at the hand-offs
When fixes keep wearing off, to find the pattern over time that brings the fault back

tasks.task: Set spare parts and consumables stock levels

items.when: When you need the list of spares each machine is likely to need, drawn from its history
When you have usage numbers, to set safety stock and reorder points for parts and consumables

tasks.task: Build and track the yearly maintenance budget

items.when: When you have past spend, to phase next year's maintenance budget by month
When big replacements may fall in the year and need a figure in the budget
When the owner sets a cap, to show two budgets that place different bets and what each drops
When actual spend drifts from budget, to show what moved, why, and a short note for the owner

tasks.task: Report maintenance numbers each month

items.when: Before building a report, to pick the few measures the reader uses to decide
When the same numbers are needed every month and should be rerun, not rebuilt
When work orders and checks are dated rows and you need monthly counts and rates
When the export is messy, to clean and reconcile it before any number is quoted

tasks.task: Write maintenance procedures and brief staff on them

items.when: When a task lives in one person's head, to get the steps, who does what and the edge cases
When a new procedure must be tested for gaps and taught to a crew
When a new check routine starts, to explain the change to staff in plain words
When old procedures exist, to find missing owners, stale pages and gaps
On a schedule, to flag procedures that no longer match how the work is done

tasks.task: Plan the response to a major failure on site

items.when: When a serious failure has happened, to plan who to tell, who investigates and what to fix
When out-of-hours call-outs depend on one phone, to set fallback contacts and switch triggers
After the event, to turn the timeline into a no-blame report and a safer procedure
When writing the plan, to test hand-offs, warnings and what happens when a step is missed

tasks.task: Hand over open repairs when a person or contractor changes

items.when: When open repairs pass to someone new, to give a job-by-job handover with access notes
Before the handover is sent, to check overdue decisions and closure proof are listed

always.when: Before any register, calendar or review is handed over, to read it as the client and list fixes
Before a sheet is printed or shared, to catch typos and an asset named two ways

helpers.when: When the job needs risk assessments, permits to work or safe systems of work written
When a large service contract goes out to several suppliers or energy bills need a tariff check
When repairs involve tenants, landlords or lease duties, not only the client's own site
When the register or log needs formulas, lookups or a dashboard beyond a simple sheet
When fault reports and check sheets should flow into the maintenance tool without retyping
When a replacement needs a full cost case with depreciation, finance and tax treatment

gaps: No library item builds an asset or vehicle register; only the kit skill covers it (the one library register is for accounting depreciation)
No library item builds a statutory checks calendar for a site: fire alarm, emergency lighting, lifts, gas, electrical and water
No library item covers legionella control: temperature logs, flushing records or a written scheme summary
No library item writes daily equipment check sheets or a driver walkaround check with defect reporting
No library item covers contractor control on site: induction, permits to work, isolation and method statements
No library item sorts an overdue maintenance backlog by risk into do, reschedule and drop
No library item reports maintenance measures such as planned work done on time, downtime and repeat faults
No library item helps set up or fill a CMMS or fleet tool: import sheets, asset hierarchy and task lists
No library item tracks fuel use, mileage, tyres and driver defects for a small fleet
No library item covers building energy use, cleaning schedules, or planning an office or workshop move
No library item offers two or three clearly different check sheet layouts to test with the crew
